topics.label: Lecture introduction and overview of cancer hallmarks
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the lecture objectives, learning outcomes, and framework for understanding the hallmarks of cancer.

topics.label: Growth signal autonomy and signaling pathway mutations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how mutations in signaling pathways such as Wnt/beta-catenin and receptor tyrosine kinases drive cell proliferation and survival independently of external growth signals.

topics.label: Block to terminal differentiation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how cancer cells in hematopoietic lineages and intestinal epithelium fail to undergo terminal differentiation while maintaining proliferative capacity.

topics.label: Resistance to apoptosis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details how mutations altering p53 activity and Bcl-2 family protein balance allow cancer cells to evade programmed cell death.

topics.label: Replicative immortality, senescence, and genome protection
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss how telomere dynamics, cellular senescence, and p53 stress responses regulate cellular lifespan, and how cancer cells bypass these barriers to achieve unlimited replication.

topics.label: Cancer metabolism and metabolic rewiring
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how cancer cells alter metabolic pathways through aerobic glycolysis, Krebs cycle mutations, and oncometabolite production.

topics.label: Induction of tumor angiogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines the necessity and mechanisms of new blood vessel formation to supply oxygen and nutrients to growing tumors.

topics.label: Mechanisms, monitoring, and genetics of metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover the multi-step cascade of cancer invasion and metastasis, including circulatory transport, liquid biopsy monitoring, metastatic inefficiency, and genomic duplication.

topics.label: Concluding remarks and summary
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session with final remarks on the integration of cancer hallmarks and recommended reading.
